title: Optimizing a Single-Session Intervention for Depression using Ecological Momentary Interventions
summary: This study examines how depressive symptoms affect people’s daily lives and how individuals perceive their symptoms. First, there is a one-time informational session on depressive symptoms, during which participants are informed about risk factors and learn to view depressive symptoms as the body’s functional signals that indicate unmet needs and call for behavioral change. Participants are then randomly assigned to two different groups. In the intervention group, participants receive brief interventions twice daily over a two-week period to help them apply the content of the session to their daily lives. In the control group, participants receive short questionnaires over the same period to measure the progression of their symptoms.

interventions.name: Intervention group: A single educational session (45 min) focusing on optimizing expectations (depressive symptoms as signals from the body) and providing information about various risk factors for depression (biological, psychological, and social factors).
